newsitem.title: USA: DC delegate slams control board's first actions.
newsitem.headline: DC delegate slams control board's first actions.

text.p: The District of Columbia's delegate to Congress Tuesday slammed the city's control board for overreaching its authority in its first steps under the new federal D.C. revitalization law.

"I am astonished that instead of starting the process in a spirit of collaboration, the control board has issued an imperial order that sets a deeply adversarial tone," Eleanor Holmes Norton, a Democrat, said in a press statement.

President Clinton earlier Tuesday signed the National Capital Revitalization Act passed by Congress last week. The measure seeks major management reforms for D.C. and turns over extensive control of city operations to the five-member control board.
For instance, the law requires the control board to develop management reform plans within 90 days for nine embattled D.C. departments.

Earlier Tuesday, the board named temporary heads for nine embattled city departments. And in a move that angered protestors, the board said deparment heads will report directly to the control board, not the mayor, "with respect to all duties."
Critics said the move exceeds the board's authority.
Norton said even Congress' "harsh" language in the new revitalization law does not stipulate a "takeover" of day-to-day operations of D.C. government.
"With some greater thought, it should have been possible for the control board to devise a way to proceed without reducing the Mayor to a mere consultative role," Norton said.
